lead: Six publications this week came from four units. Biology has two: Joe Bennett on conservation planning for eastern Canadian birds, and Ashkan Golshani on a lupin reference genome. Computer Science has two (Edward Melcer on game-based clinical exams, Evangelos Kranakis on robot search), Earth Sciences has one (Hillary Maddin on Carboniferous tetrapods), and Physics has one (Razvan Gornea, as part of the large nEXO collaboration). Each paper lists a single Carleton author, so no cross-unit collaborations within Carleton are evident this week. Four of the six are preprints or repository postings (bioRxiv, Zenodo, and two on arXiv).

items.title: Chromosome-scale reference assembly of New World lupin Lupinus mexicanus
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary: The authors assembled a chromosome-scale reference genome for Lupinus mexicanus, a lupin native to central Mexico. The assembly spans 837 Mb on 24 chromosomes and includes 36,575 protein-coding genes. It gives researchers a resource for studying New World lupins, which are less studied than Old World species, as potential high-protein crops.

items.title: Comparing Game-Based and Virtual Objective Structured Clinical Examination Formats: Perceived Fairness and Achievement Emotions in Clinical Competency Examinations for Low- and Middle-Income Countries
items.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
items.summary: This study compared a digital game-based assessment platform (ENTRUST) with virtual in-person-style clinical exams (OSCEs) during a high-stakes surgical certification exam for trainees across sub-Saharan Africa. Examinees reported lower anxiety, higher enjoyment and stronger perceptions of fairness with the game-based format, and the authors conclude that how an assessment is designed shapes how fair and stressful it feels.

items.title: Estimation of body-mass distributions of Carboniferous tetrapod communities and comparison with modern coastal tropical wetlands
items.summary: The authors estimated body masses for 21 tetrapods from Pennsylvanian sites at Joggins and Point Aconi, Nova Scotia, using the surface area of vertebrae, and compared the size distributions with modern coastal tropical wetland communities. They conclude that bias in which animals get preserved explains some of the differences, and that the limited range of diets among Carboniferous tetrapods may explain others.

opportunities.heading: Game-based surgical exam rated fairer and less stressful than virtual OSCEs
opportunities.what: Melcer's team compared the ENTRUST game-based platform with virtual OSCEs in a surgical certification exam. Examinees reported lower anxiety, more enjoyment and stronger perceptions of fairness with ENTRUST.
opportunities.market_fit: Certification bodies, medical boards and exam vendors already buy assessment delivery. Oral and OSCE exams are costly and resource intensive. ENTRUST is positioned as an alternative format.

partners.name: Prometric
partners.why: Large exam vendor with a VR skills and simulation assessment offering.

partners.name: Intuitive Surgical
partners.why: Already linked to ENTRUST through its surgical education learners forum.

opportunities.next_step: Call Melcer and Dana Lin at Stanford first to settle who owns ENTRUST IP. Then approach an assessment vendor with a Mitacs Accelerate or NSERC Alliance proposal. Stanford is a co-owner.
opportunities.licensing_note: Partnership. Stanford leads the platform and its authoring tools. Carleton's contribution is design and evaluation know-how, so this is not a clean licence.

evidence.market: Medical certification bodies and exam vendors already pay for high-stakes assessment design and delivery.
evidence.partner: Prometric sells assessment design and delivery, including VR skills evaluation. It is operating today.
evidence.carleton_role: Melcer (Computer Science) is first author and helped create the ENTRUST platform.
evidence.evidence: ENTRUST was compared with virtual OSCEs in a real high-stakes surgical certification exam across sub-Saharan Africa.

near_misses.title: Chromosome-scale reference assembly of New World lupin Lupinus mexicanus
near_misses.why: market: No buyer identified for a wild lupin species genome. Lupin crops sold today are other species; Carleton's role: First and last authors are at Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada. Golshani is a middle author; evidence: Reference assembly only, with 98% BUSCO completeness. No crop improvement method or trait validation
